---
title: "Methods: scoring, ranking, enrichment, dedup"
---

This page walks through every analytical decision the package makes, the default
it ships, and the study that validates it. Defaults are chosen to match
community practice; every one can be overridden.

## Significance scoring {#scoring}

`pi_score()` implements the π-score of Xiao et al. (2014), which ranks hits by
**both** statistical significance and effect size rather than a p-value alone.

| Variant | Formula | Direction | Default cutoff |
|---|---|---|---|
| `eq2` (default) | $\pi = P^{|\log_2 FC|}$ | smaller = stronger | 0.05 |
| `eq1` | $\pi = |\log_2 FC|\cdot(-\log_{10}P)$ | larger = stronger | — |

The two are monotone-equivalent: $-\log_{10}(P^{|\log_2 FC|}) = |\log_2 FC|\cdot(-\log_{10}P)$,
so `eq2 < 0.05` is exactly `eq1 > 1.301`. `eq2` is reported on the familiar
p-scale.

- Xiao Y, *et al.* "A novel significance score for gene selection and ranking."
  *Bioinformatics* 2014;30(6):801–7. PMID:22321699.

## Multiple-testing correction {#adjustment}

`adjust_p()` defaults to **Benjamini–Hochberg** FDR, applied per contrast.
Alternatives: `bonferroni` (FWER), `qvalue` (Storey), `IHW` (independent
hypothesis weighting).

- Benjamini Y, Hochberg Y. *J R Stat Soc B* 1995;57(1):289–300.
- Storey JD, Tibshirani R. *PNAS* 2003;100(16):9440–5. PMID:12883005.
- Ignatiadis N, *et al.* "Data-driven hypothesis weighting (IHW)." *Nat Methods*
  2016;13:577–80. PMID:27240256.

## Gene ranking for GSEA {#ranking}

fgsea needs a **signed** per-gene statistic so up- and down-regulated genes sit
at opposite ends of the ranked list. The default is the limma/proteoDA
**moderated t-statistic** (`rank_by = "t"`).

| `rank_by` | Statistic | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| `"t"` (default) | moderated t (limma/proteoDA/DEqMS/proDA) | the input carries a `t` column |
| `"signed_p"` (fallback) | $\text{sign}(\log FC)\cdot-\log_{10}P$ | no test statistic available (e.g. edgeR) |
| `"logFC"` | effect size only | ranking by magnitude |

Why moderated t: it is the test statistic GSEA-style analyses are meant to
consume for moderated linear models, and it is what the hand-written source
pipelines use. Unsigned π-score columns are **rejected** — ranking by them
collapses the list to one tail.

- Subramanian A, *et al.* "GSEA." *PNAS* 2005;102(43):15545–50. PMID:16199517.
- Reimand J, *et al.* "Pathway enrichment analysis ... (g:Profiler, GSEA,
  Cytoscape, EnrichmentMap)." *Nat Protoc* 2019;14:482–517. PMID:30664679.
- Korotkevich G, *et al.* "Fast gene set enrichment analysis." bioRxiv 2021.
  doi:10.1101/060012.

## Enrichment {#enrichment}

`ev_enrich()` runs **fgsea** (ranked) and/or **ORA** (hypergeometric) against
registered databases. Gene-set size filters default to `min_size = 15`,
`max_size = 500` (Reimand 2019 §S3.4: sets below ~15 are noise-prone, above ~500
non-specific). `eps = 0` gives exact fgsea p-values.

## Pathway deduplication {#deduplication}

Enrichment returns many overlapping terms. `ev_collapse()` reduces redundancy
with **collection-agnostic** methods only — see the [survey](#dedup-survey) for
why GO-semantic methods are excluded.

### Methods

| `method` | What it does | Basis | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `collapse_then_jaccard` (default) | `fgsea::collapsePathways`, then set-similarity on survivors | conditional permutation + gene overlap | Korotkevich 2021; Merico 2010 |
| `collapse_fgsea` | `fgsea::collapsePathways` only | conditional permutation independence | Korotkevich 2021 |
| `jaccard` / `jaccard_then_collapse` | set-similarity (see `similarity`) | gene overlap | Merico 2010 |

### Set-similarity metric (`similarity`)

For the gene-overlap steps, choose the metric on leading-edge gene sets $A,B$:

| `similarity` | Formula | Catches | EnrichmentMap cutoff |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jaccard` (default) | $\dfrac{|A\cap B|}{|A\cup B|}$ | symmetric overlap | 0.25 |
| `overlap` | $\dfrac{|A\cap B|}{\min(|A|,|B|)}$ | a small set contained in a larger one | 0.5 |
| `combined` | $w\cdot\text{Jaccard} + (1-w)\cdot\text{Overlap}$ | both (Cytoscape default) | 0.375 |

`combined_weight` ($w$) defaults to 0.5. The package's `cutoff` default is 0.5
for all metrics (backward compatible); set it to the EnrichmentMap canonical
values above to match Cytoscape exactly.

`fgsea::collapsePathways` is a **conditional permutation independence test**
(re-runs fgsea conditioning on each candidate parent's genes; "main pathways"
are those not explained by a parent). `pval.threshold` defaults to 0.05.

### Why GO-semantic methods are not core {#dedup-survey}

| Method | Similarity basis | Works on any gene set? | Needs GO/OrgDb? |
|---|---|---|---|
| fgsea `collapsePathways` | conditional permutation | **yes** | no |
| Jaccard / Overlap / combined | gene overlap | **yes** | no |
| `clusterProfiler::simplify` | GO Wang semantic | no (hard-stops off-GO) | **yes** |
| `rrvgo` | GO Resnik/Wang semantic | no | **yes** |
| `GOSemSim`, `simplifyEnrichment` | GO semantic similarity | no / tuned-for-GO | **yes** |

`enrichVolcano` spans Hallmark, Reactome, KEGG, MitoCarta, CORUM and GO across
seven species and does **not** assume a GO OrgDb is installed, so it ships only
the collection-agnostic methods (rows 1–2). GO-semantic collapse remains an
optional, GO-only enhancement.

- Merico D, *et al.* "Enrichment Map." *PLoS One* 2010;5(11):e13984. PMID:21085593.
- Yu G, *et al.* "clusterProfiler." *OMICS* 2012;16(5):284–7. PMID:22455463.
- Yu G, *et al.* "GOSemSim." *Bioinformatics* 2010;26(7):976–8. PMID:20179076.
- Gu Z, Hübschmann D. "simplifyEnrichment." *GPB* 2022. PMID:37670900.

## Databases {#databases}

`list_databases()` enumerates the registered collections; `database_info(name)`
prints provenance, license and citation. Hallmark is the curated,
minimally-redundant collection recommended as a first lens (Liberzon 2015,
PMID:26771021).
